**Technique:** The draft includes a provenance footer listing the specific evidence rows it used. If the draft says 'built a retrieval pipeline with 95% recall,' the footer shows which project record in the ledger supports that claim. This makes the review faster and more accurate.

sections.title: Gap identification and remediation
sections.body:
Before applying, the system identifies gaps between the opportunity requirements and the candidate's evidence ledger. Gaps are classified: hard gap (candidate does not have the experience, period), soft gap (candidate has partial or adjacent experience), training gap (candidate could acquire the skill before the role starts), and documentation gap (candidate has the experience but it is not recorded in the ledger).

**Remediation plan (synthesized):** For each gap, the system proposes: (1) For soft gaps — frame adjacent experience that demonstrates transferable skills. (2) For training gaps — suggest a short learning path with estimated duration. (3) For documentation gaps — log which project record needs updating. The candidate decides which gaps to address and how.

sections.title: Interview preparation workflow
sections.body:
Interview preparation follows a structured cycle: (1) Analyze the role's stated requirements and typical interview format (technical screen, system design, behavioral, case study). (2) Extract likely question categories from the role description and industry patterns. (3) For each category, draft responses using the evidence ledger. (4) Review responses for accuracy, conciseness, and appropriate disclosure. (5) Practice responses (candidate-owned) and iterate based on self-assessment.

**Synthesized example:** For a Staff Engineer role requiring distributed systems experience, the preparation workflow would identify relevant projects from the ledger (e.g., 'design a distributed retrieval pipeline with idempotency guarantees'), draft a structured response covering problem, approach, tradeoffs, and outcome, and flag any limitations (e.g., 'the pipeline handled 1,000 QPS in load testing but was not tested at production scale').

sections.title: Cover letter composition
sections.body:
A cover letter is a projection from the evidence ledger to a specific opportunity. It should: (1) name the role and organization, (2) connect a specific evidence row to a specific requirement, (3) demonstrate understanding of the organization's context, (4) state what the candidate would bring, and (5) close with a forward-looking statement.

**Synthesized example structure:** 'I am writing about the **[role]** at **[org]**. My experience with **[project from ledger]** involved **[relevant skill]** to achieve **[measured outcome]**, which aligns with your need for **[stated requirement]**. I have followed **[org]**'s work on **[topic]** and would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background matches your team's goals.'

**Boundary:** The draft must be reviewed for accuracy. No claim should appear in the letter that is not supported by the evidence ledger. The provenance footer linking each sentence to its evidence row enables this review.

sections.title: Salary and offer research
sections.body:
Salary research follows a structured process: (1) Identify the role level and geography. (2) Gather data from multiple sources (levels.fyi, Glassdoor, Blind, company disclosures, recruiter ranges). (3) Record each data point with source and date. (4) Build a range: minimum acceptable, target, and aspirational. (5) Prepare talking points that tie the target to evidence (experience level, market rate, specific qualifications).

**Technique:** Maintain a salary research log with entries per opportunity. Each entry records: role, level, geography, sources consulted, range found, date of research, and any time sensitivity (e.g., 'this range may shift with the start of the new fiscal year').

**Boundary:** Salary research informs negotiation preparation. It does not predict what any specific employer will offer, and it should not be used to anchor expectations prematurely.

sections.title: The evidence preparation cycle completed
sections.body:
The full cycle from opportunity identification to submission readiness is: (1) Identify and record opportunity with source and date. (2) Research role, company, and compensation. (3) Audit evidence ledger for match and gaps. (4) Address gaps (update ledger, acquire training, or accept the gap). (5) Draft application materials from selected evidence. (6) Review for accuracy, privacy, and authorization. (7) Hold for human release.

**History preservation:** Each cycle produces a record: opportunity researched, materials prepared, gaps identified, and decisions made (applied, passed, declined). This record supports future cycles by accumulating evidence of past preparation patterns.

**Boundary:** The cycle supports human decision-making. No step in the cycle submits an application, sends a message, or modifies a public profile without explicit per-action human authorization.

limit: Employment Operations is described here as a local-first preparation and review system. This page does not expose personal data or claim automated outreach, application submission, hiring outcomes, legal guidance or active provider integration. Synthetic examples are pedagogical only.
